On The 5 th Of March, 2026
 Misc. Appeal No. 2659 of 2019
 Ganpatlal S/O Suratram Patidar
 Versus
 Karulal S/O Nanuram Balai
 And Two Others
Appearance:
Appellant - Original Claimant by Shri Pourush Ranka - A  None appears for respondents No.1 and 2 - Driver and Ow  offending vehicle.
Respondent No.3 - Insurance Company by Shri Manoj Jain   Advocate.
ORDER With the consent of learned counsel appearing for the parties, the matter is heard finally.

The appellant has filed this appeal under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (herein after referred to as the Act of 1988) being aggrieved by award dated 08.02.2019 (Annexure A/1)
passed by learned Second Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Mandsaur, District Mandsaur (MP) in Motor Accident Claim Case No.15 of 2018, whereby challenging the quantum of compensation.

entities.label: COURT

entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:
2. Short facts of the case are that the appellant was going to give food NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-IND:6089 2 MA-2659-2019 to one of his relatives in hospital on 18.07.2016 by motorcycle from Village Gurjar Bardiya to Mandsaur and when he reached near Sitamau Gate, in front of Agriculture College, respondent No.1 came driving Maruti Omni Car bearing registration number MP-14 BE-0278 in rash and negligent manner coming from the wrong side and dashed into the motorcycle of the appellant, because of which, he sustained grievous injuries.
His left leg was fractured from two places.
He sustained fractures in Tibia Fibula and Femur bones of his left leg.

He was immediately rushed to District Hospital, Mandsaur (MP), where he was given primary treatment and thereafter he was referred to Sunrise Hospital, Udaipur (Rajasthan) where he was operated upon at his left leg on two places.
He remained hospitalized for a period of fifteen days.
The appellant sustained permanent disability because of the injuries sustained in his left leg on account of the road accident.

He filed a claim petition under Sections 166 and 140 of the Act of 1988 Ganpatlal vs Karulal on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84695741/
1 for the injuries sustained by him.

3. The Claims Tribunal, after recording evidence, concluded that the accident occurred due to fault of driver of the insured vehicle, thus awarded a total compensation of Rs.2,94,400/- (rupees two lakh ninety four thousand four hundred only).

The Tribunal, while quantifying the compensation,
has treated income of the appellant as Rs.4,500/- per month and Permanent Disability was treated at 10% of the overall body.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that on three counts the amount of compensation is inadequate.

First, Permanent Disability was proved to the extent of 22% by Exhibit P/82 - Permanent Disability NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:6089 3 MA-2659-2019 Certificate; second, the income of the appellant was assessed at Rs.4,500/- per month, which is much less than even the minimum wages at the relevant time on the date of accident, which is Rs.6,850/- per month; and third, that the Tribunal has not added anything under the Head of Future Prospects, when indisputably the age of the appellant at the time of accident was 38 years.

entities.text: Permanent Disability NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:6089 3 MA-2659-2019 Certificate
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: He thus prays for enhancement of compensation amount.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.3 - Insurance Company submits that 22%
Permanent Disability was certified by the doctor only with respect to left lower limb, which cannot be treated as 22% with respect to overall body.
Thus, the Tribunal has not committed any mistake in this regard.
5.1 With regard to income of the appellant, learned counsel submits that as the claimant did not prove his income by any material, thus the Tribunal has correctly assessed his income.
5.2 As regards Future Prospects, he submits that the appellant has suffered only fractures, thus there was no need to add any amount towards Future Prospects in the income of the appellant.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7.
A perusal of the record would shows that doctor certified Permanent Disability of the appellant vide Exhibit P/82 at 22%.

The Tribunal considered the same and statement of the expert witness,
Dr. P.K. Upadhyaya (PW-3), who also deposed and said that the appellant had suffered 22%
Permanent Disability at left lower limb.

8. Considering the nature of work which was claimed by the appellant NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-IND:6089 4 MA-2659-2019 inasmuch as he was doing business of selling bangles and agricultural work, 22% Permanent Disability in his left lower limb must have made him incapable to a great extent in continuing with his agricultural work and even selling bangles; as such, by applying the test, as laid down by the Apex Court in case of Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar reported in (2011) 2 SCC 343 , overall Permanent Disability of the appellant is treated at 15%.

entities.text: Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar reported in (2011) 2 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 9. As regards the income of the appellant, it is seen that the Claims Tribunal after disbelieving the claim of the appellant had treated his income of Rs.4,500/- per month, however, there is no Ganpatlal vs Karulal on 5 March, 2026

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84695741/
2 reference material for arriving this income, only it has been mentioned that notional income of a labour in the year 2016 can be treated as Rs.4,500/-, which in the considered view of this Court is not correct, in view of the fact that the State Legal Services Authority has provided that at the relevant time minimum wages for an unskilled labourer were Rs.6,850/- per month, as such, the same is treated as the income of the appellant.

10. In view of the law, as laid down by the Apex Court in case of National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and others reported in 2017 (16) SCC 680 , 40% addition towards Future Prospects in the income of the appellant is made, considering his age which is found at 38 years at the time of accident, as such the amount of compensation will be changed; and now there will be a differential amount of Rs.1,82,630/- (rupees one lakh eighty two thousand six hundred thirty only)
which is to be paid to the appellant, over and above the amount of compensation which has already been granted by the Claims Tribunal.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and others reported in 2017 (16) SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, the enhanced amount shall NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:6089 5 MA-2659-2019 carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of application filed before the Claims Tribunal i..e. 15.09.2016 till its payment.
Other terms and conditions of the impugned award shall remain intact.

10.1 It is seen from the record that the appeal is valued at Rs.1,00,000/- (rupees one lakh only), as such, the appellant is directed to pay differential Court Fee within a period of four weeks from today.
11. With the aforesaid, this miscellaneous appeal is partly allowed and disposed off.
Pending interlocutory application, if any, also stands disposed off.
(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE rcp Ganpatlal vs Karulal on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84695741/
